next.prompt: Welcome: an optional way to give extra context about the graph direction or the initial hook, beside the subject field. Default behaviour unchanged (type a title, press Enter). Start from the final welcome recipe (agent_design/welcome/RECIPE.md) and the user's sketch in refs/. Explore structurally different mechanisms.

Rule for every round to come, alway true: keep the current app v0.1.0 welcome design as a base. We will end up very close.
I like the shift + enter mecanics to trigger the optionnal text filed

"Carry the lantern in" button
- only shows up when text field cursor became/is active
- on shift + enter it relocate in a cool travel animation (make one with reduce/collapse -> travel -> grow/settle, some morphing maybe. for the other two you propose the animation)

nodes.title: Second line
nodes.direction: Always visible: a quiet optional 'Direction' writing line sits under the subject field, so context is one tab away and never has to be discovered.

nodes.title: Add direction
nodes.direction: Disclosure: a quiet 'Add direction' control among the tone and model controls opens a panel under the field, with 'Start from…', 'Aim at…', 'I already know…' stubs; a suggestion chip can carry its hook into it.

nodes.title: One field, two lines
nodes.direction: No new control: the subject field itself grows. Enter submits, Shift+Enter starts a second part; line one is the subject, the rest is the direction. Pasting a multi-line brief just works.

nodes.title: Second underline
nodes.direction: Shift+Enter in the subject opens a second, smaller underline under it, the same writing gesture one size down. The v0.1.0 hall is otherwise untouched; the button stays centred below.

nodes.title: Capsule
nodes.direction: Your sketch: while you type, the subject becomes a capsule with Carry the lantern in docked inside it. Shift+Enter grows the capsule downward into a two-part card, subject above a hairline, direction below, button still docked.

nodes.title: Folding note
nodes.direction: Shift+Enter opens the direction under the subject like 01, but once you leave it, it folds into a one-line note (↳ Start from the physics…) under the subject; click or Shift+Enter unfolds it.

nodes.title: Fold and carry
nodes.direction: Your choreography: the button folds into a circle, then a lit dot, swings out along an arc to its new dock, and unfolds back into the pill with a small overshoot. Appearing on focus is the same unfold from a dot; leaving folds it away.

nodes.title: Ember carry
nodes.direction: The button speaks the Welcome ember language: it flares, dissolves into embers, a light carries it to the new dock (the same travelling light as arrival and submit) and it re-lights there with a soft halo. Focus lights it the same way, a light running along the capsule's lower edge into it.

nodes.title: Ride the edge
nodes.direction: No travel at all: the button is pinned to the capsule's corner and rides its edge as the capsule grows, with a small elastic overshoot and a squash on landing; the hairline draws in behind it. On focus the button slides out from behind the capsule's right edge.

nodes.title: Ride, settle
nodes.direction: r003-03 without the bounce: the capsule grows and the pinned button rides its corner on a plain ease-out (380 ms), stopping dead at its dock. No overshoot, no squash; slide in/out and the hairline unchanged.

nodes.title: Ride, glide
nodes.direction: The same ride on a symmetric ease-in-out (480 ms): the card opens like a drawer, accelerating and decelerating evenly, the button travelling with the corner. The calmest and most deliberate of the three.

nodes.title: Ride, snap
nodes.direction: The same ride, quick: ease-out-quint over 240 ms, so the card is open almost before the key comes up. Motion as confirmation only, the least visible of the three.
